scenes.line1: How does Git track your code?
scenes.say: Ever wondered how Git keeps track of your code and changes? What's the deal with HEAD and remote tracking?

scenes.label: Commit
scenes.sub: A commit saves your code at a moment in time.
scenes.say: A commit is a snapshot. It saves your code exactly as it is right now.
Branches are pointers to commits. HEAD marks the branch you're working on. Remote branches track code on another repository.

scenes.title: Branching & Tracking
scenes.say: You create a branch, switch to it, and fetch updates from the remote repository. This keeps your local code in sync.

scenes.question: What does HEAD point to in Git?
scenes.wrong: HEAD is always the latest commit.
scenes.right: HEAD points to your current branch and commit. It's where new commits go.
scenes.say: Here's a classic interview trap: What does HEAD point to in Git? It's not always the latest commit. HEAD marks your current branch and commit—where your next changes will land.
